prompt: Edit this exact 2 by 2 grid of the ORIGINAL upper half of one pixel-art woman's portrait into a subtle, believable skeptical expression with blinking phases. Treat the supplied original as the authoritative geometry, palette and texture. Keep hair, forehead, nose bridge, head silhouette, crop, background and all four cell positions identical. Keep both eyes in their original sockets, original size and spacing. Keep pupils facing straight at the viewer, symmetric and naturally centered; do not make a side glance or rolled eyes. Skepticism comes from a SMALL natural eyebrow asymmetry: one eyebrow rises only approximately ONE native pixel, the other remains relaxed near its original position, with slightly questioning upper lids. NO exaggerated arches, NO sharp scowl, NO dark eyeliner, NO huge contrast, NO smug cartoon stare. Both brows must remain clearly visible and softly shaded like the original. Row-major cell order: top-left open skeptical eyes; top-right half-closed blink; bottom-left fully closed blink; bottom-right exact repeat of top-left open. The same eyebrow shapes and positions in every cell: only lids move for blinking. Closed eyes are fully closed, with a soft thin lid line. Half closed really covers about half the iris. Preserve the low-resolution soft muted pixel-art texture; no crisp vector edges or airbrushed smearing, no eyelashes or details beyond original style. Do not change face proportions or tilt the head. Output the entire 2x2 sheet with the same landscape aspect ratio, no labels, no padding, no border.
